towns.roads: US-278 is the only road on and off Hilton Head Island, crossing to the mainland over the Mackay Creek and Skull Creek bridges. A single serious crash on that corridor has no alternate route to absorb it, and back-ups extend for miles in both directions. On-island, William Hilton Parkway carries the bulk of resident, worker and visitor traffic past commercial frontage with frequent turning movements, while the Sea Pines Circle rotary concentrates unfamiliar seasonal drivers into a single high-conflict junction. towns.content:
Hilton Head Island's crash profile is unlike anywhere else in South Carolina, because the island has exactly one road on and off it. US-278 carries every resident, worker, delivery vehicle and visitor across the bridges at Mackay Creek and Skull Creek, and when a serious crash closes that corridor there is no alternate route.

A large share of injuries here happen to people who do not live in South Carolina, and that creates two practical problems. Treatment begins on the island and continues somewhere else entirely, leaving a medical record split across two states that has to be assembled rather than simply requested. And the insurance policies that matter are frequently out of state, which raises the question of whether a distant adjuster is entitled to interpret South Carolina coverage on its own terms.

South Carolina law governs the claim regardless of where the injured person lives, and it permits stacking of uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage — often worth considerably more than an out-of-state insurer's first assessment suggests.

faqs.question: Where would my Hilton Head injury case be filed?
faqs.answer: In the Beaufort County Court of Common Pleas at 102 Ribaut Rd. in Beaufort, roughly 40 miles off-island. Complaints go through South Carolina's mandatory Tyler Odyssey e-filing system, and most cases are routed to mediation before trial under SC ADR Rule 3.

faqs.question: Is there a trauma centre on Hilton Head Island?
faqs.answer: No. The island has no DPH-designated trauma centre, so seriously injured patients are stabilised locally and transported off-island. That transfer lengthens the treatment record and makes early preservation of EMS and transfer documentation important to the claim.

faqs.question: I was injured on holiday — does South Carolina law apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. South Carolina law governs a crash that happens here regardless of where you live, and it permits stacking of uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage. That often decides the real value of a claim against a minimum-limits local driver, so every applicable policy should be identified before anything is settled.
